title: Mouse movement
help: Sends a relative movement with Windows SendInput. Positive X moves right; positive Y moves down. Delay postpones the start. Duration 0 or one step sends the whole motion at once; multiple steps distribute the exact total ΔX/ΔY across the duration. For one action per key press, use If key down → On new press. For repeated motion while held, choose While held and Repeat until stopped. A second block with negative deltas can reverse the motion after a Wait. This does not measure or set a game's camera position. Stop with Ctrl+Alt+F7. Use macros only where permitted.

title: Recognize text
hint: Local OCR for images and PDF
help: Reads PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, WebP or PDF locally and stores the result in a variable. PDF pages are rendered in grayscale at 200 DPI and passed to Tesseract. Set PDF page to 1–100 for one page or 0 for all pages (up to 20). GIF and WebP work when the installed Tesseract build includes the matching Leptonica decoders. If the engine or language is missing, the first run offers to download the 64-bit UB Mannheim Tesseract 5.5.3 Windows build from the Tesseract GitHub release (about 24.1 MiB / 25.3 MB) and only the models named in the language field; no network request is made without explicit consent. After consent, Windows UAC asks to approve the installer; confirm the prompt to install Tesseract in LocalAppData\KLIKER Blocks\Tesseract-OCR. The app verifies the engine and continues without a restart. If UAC is declined or permission is unavailable, setup stops; you can enter the path to an existing tesseract.exe instead. Engine and file paths containing Cyrillic characters use Windows short names when available. Files are never sent over the network. Automatic setup is unavailable on 32-bit Windows. Limits: 32 MiB PDF/input, 32 MiB rendered page image, 100000 output characters and 1–120 seconds total timeout. Password-protected PDFs cannot be OCRed without a password. Example: set the PDF path to scan.pdf and PDF page to 0; Recognize text reads up to 20 pages into ocr_text, separating page results with a page break. Small or blurry text may be misread.
